note:
mail: seven definitions spelled with a verb §2.4 abolishes, renamed to the canonical one.

Three are the fetchmail polling family, which are not reads at all -- they poll a mailbox and write records -- so they take the domain verb the module already used for the single-server pass (_poll_mailbox): fetch_mail -> action_poll_mailbox (the "Fetch Now" button, action_ per §2.4 for a new button method), _fetch_mails -> _poll_due_mailboxes (the cron entry point) and _fetch_mail -> _poll_mailboxes (the recordset loop, overridden in enterprise/l10n_cl_edi and renamed there in the same change).

The other four: _fetch_twilio_ice_servers -> _get_twilio_ice_servers (a read), _delete_and_notify -> _remove_and_notify and _delete_inactive_rtc_sessions -> _remove_inactive_rtc_sessions (business removals, not the ORM operation), and _verify_vapid_public_key -> _is_vapid_public_key_current, which §2.4.8 settles the other way from the table hint: it returns a bool and never raises, so it is a predicate, not _check_.

ADR-0056 named _fetch_mails as the open case of a method whose name is written into ir_act_server.code, and mail ships that cron under noupdate="1" -- so an upgraded database keeps the old string. addons/mail/migrations/1.26/pre-migration.py rewrites it, and the other renames, in ir_act_server.code and ir_actions_server_history.code, on Postgres word boundaries. Three renames are deliberately not in that script: _compute_im_status, _compute_activity_summary and _default_activity_type are still live names on other models.

95 -> 88.

Command: python tooling/architecture/naming_vocabulary.py --count
